title: The High Rivergate
premise: Rafael Villalobos, a desert ranger chasing a thief who stole his late partner's compass, is forced to team up with the very crew of scavengers he once called family before a bitter falling-out. Their old rival, Captain Ilsa Reyes, hires them for a salvage run to the High Rivergate — a drowned city wreck they all swore never to touch, where Rafael's debt and his grief are buried together. Racing a rival salvage fleet and the monsoon, six tides from landfall, the crew must dive the flooded gates while old betrayals resurface and the compass reveals it was never a navigation tool but a key. In the end, Rafael chooses his found family over the treasure that could clear his debt, sinking the gate's power source forever and earning back the belonging he threw away.
about_author: Mara Nakamura is the pen name of a former maritime archaeologist who spent five years cataloguing wrecks off monsoon-battered coastlines before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels about stubborn people, salt water, and the families we build when our first ones fail us.

chapters.title: Nothing but Sand and a Debt
chapters.summary: Rafael Villalobos tracks a thief across the empty flats and corners him at a waystation, only to recover not money but his dead partner's brass compass — which points somewhere impossible. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: grim determination curdling into unease as the past refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Crew That Wasn't
chapters.summary: The compass leads Rafael to a harbor town where his old crew — engineer Sefa, diver Tomás, quartermaster Odile — are scraping by after he abandoned them three years ago. They want nothing to do with him until Captain Ilsa Reyes arrives with a contract for the High Rivergate. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: shame and longing tangled together.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Ilsa lays out the stakes: a rival salvage fleet leaves in two days, and the monsoon makes the wreck undivable in six tides. The job pays enough to erase Rafael's debt — if the crew takes him back. Tomás votes no; Sefa votes yes; Odile breaks the tie. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: wary hope outweighing resentment.

chapters.title: Salt in Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Aboard Ilsa's ship, the crew relearns how to work together while Rafael and Tomás clash over an old betrayal neither will name. A night storm forces them to trust each other or lose the rigging. POV: Tomás. Emotional beat: anger softening into grudging respect.

chapters.title: The Drowned Gate
chapters.summary: They reach the High Rivergate at slack tide and make first descent through its flooded archways, finding the city eerily preserved — and signs the rival fleet arrived early. Rafael's compass begins pulling toward something below. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: What the Compass Knows
chapters.summary: Sefa deciphers the compass: it's a key to the gate's tide-engine, a power source worth fortunes — and capable of drowning coastlines. Rafael realizes his partner died trying to hide it here. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: wonder giving way to moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Boarded
chapters.summary: The rival fleet's captain, Voss, boards Ilsa's ship under flag of parley and offers to buy the compass; when refused, he takes Tomás hostage and gives them two tides. Odile proposes a desperate plan using the gate's own currents. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: fear forged into resolve.

chapters.title: Two Tides Down
chapters.summary: The crew dives the engine chamber under Voss's guns, fighting current and his divers alike. Tomás saves Rafael's life instead of escaping, finally naming the old betrayal — Rafael left him behind on their last dive. POV: Tomás. Emotional beat: rupture and reconciliation in one breath.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Climax: as the monsoon hits, Rafael holds the compass-key at the engine's heart and must choose — take the fortune that clears his debt, or collapse the gate and drown the power forever. He sinks it, nearly with himself, and the crew pulls him out. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: sacrifice answering grief.

chapters.title: Home Water
chapters.summary: Aftermath: debt unpaid but debts of honor settled, the crew refuses Ilsa's next contract and buys a small boat of their own. Rafael asks, formally, to come home — and Odile hands him a berth roster with his name already on it. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won belonging.
